correctness.rationale: On [0,1] f_r(x)=sin(pi x)/(1+rx) has fixed 0 (derivative pi) and exactly one positive fixed point by monotonic sin(pi x)/x and 1/(1+rx). Its multiplier crosses -1 at c=acos(-1/pi)/pi, r*=(sin(pi c)-c)/c². For any distinct two-cycle x<y, equality H(x)=H(y) for H(t)=t+sin(pi t), strict concavity and midpoint m(d)=acos[-d/sin(pi d)]/pi reduce full problem to scalar F(d,r). Its proved strict negative derivative for 0<=r<=r* and strictly negative endpoint at the boundary produce exactly one root below r*, none at/above. Even Taylor expansion yields d~sqrt((r*-r)/C), C>0, and critical flip normal form gives return multiplier 1-4k(r*-r)+O((r*-r)^1.5), k>0. Independent high precision values at representative parameters and near r* checked r*~0.94810546376 and asymptotic multipliers. Sampling was not used for exhaustive root count.
